questions.prompt: The users table and password handling conventions:
options: email UNIQUE (violations → 409) · password VARCHAR(255) for bcrypt · default role 'member' · password_hash() to store, password_verify(plain, storedHash) to check
email indexed only · password VARCHAR(32) · default role 'admin' · md5() to store, strcmp to check
username UNIQUE · password TEXT plaintext · role enum('root') · base64 encode
email PRIMARY KEY · password CHAR(60) · role nullable · sha1 + salt column
questions.explain: **UNIQUE email** = one account per address (duplicate → 409 in register). bcrypt hashes are long → **VARCHAR(255)** (truncation silently breaks verify!). New users are **member**; admin assigned explicitly. `password_hash($plain, PASSWORD_DEFAULT)` → `$2y$...`; `password_verify(plain, hash)` — that argument order.

questions.prompt: Building the token payload: which claims and signing call?
options: sub = user id, exp = $now + ttl · JWT::encode($payload, $secret, 'HS256')
uid = email, ttl = 3600 · JWT::sign($payload)
user = full row, never expires · hash_hmac('md5', ...)
sub = role, exp = $now − ttl · base64_encode($payload)
questions.explain: **sub** (subject) = user id; **exp** = issued time + TTL seconds (3600 default). `JWT::encode($payload, $secret, 'HS256')` signs. Decoding requires `new Key($this->secret, $this->algo)` — the Key pins the secret AND the algorithm (stops algorithm-swap attacks).

questions.prompt: The auth middleware reads the token from the request with:
options: getHeaderLine('Authorization') matched against /^Bearer\s+(.+)$/i, token = $m[1]; invalid/missing → 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
$_COOKIE['jwt'] directly; invalid → 500
getParsedBody()['token']; invalid → 200 with error flag
The URL query ?token=...; invalid → redirect to /login
questions.explain: PSR-7: **getHeaderLine** reads the header string; the regex matches the **Bearer scheme** (capture group 1 = raw token). On success the payload is attached with **withAttribute** (immutable request → returns a NEW one). Missing/invalid → **401** + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

questions.prompt: Protecting routes and checking roles in Slim:
options: ->add($auth) on a route or whole group · handler reads getAttribute('auth') and checks $auth['role'] · wrong role → 403
Global if-statement in index.php · check $_SESSION['role'] · wrong role → 401
JavaScript guard on the frontend only
->middleware('auth') · check $request->role · wrong role → 404
questions.explain: `->add($auth)` attaches middleware to one route or a **whole group** (POST/PUT/DELETE gated at once). The handler reads what the middleware attached: `getAttribute('auth')` → `$auth['role']` (baked into the token at login). Authenticated but not allowed → **403 Forbidden** (401 would mean no/invalid token).

questions.prompt: Which PHP function checks a login attempt against the stored bcrypt hash? (function name)
questions.explain: **`password_verify($plain, $storedHash)`** — plain attempt first, stored hash second. Storing uses `password_hash($plain, PASSWORD_DEFAULT)`.

questions.prompt: Why must the password column be VARCHAR(255) rather than VARCHAR(32)?
options: bcrypt output is ~60 chars and future algorithms may be longer — a short column TRUNCATES the hash and password_verify silently fails forever
Long passwords need long columns
MySQL requires 255 for indexes
It compresses better
questions.explain: The stored value is the **hash**, not the password. Truncate it and every future verify fails with no error — the classic silent-death bug. 255 is the lab's size.
